text:
olivia: Hey all — I addressed the review comments from yesterday and split the retry logic into a RetryPolicy type, added unit tests, and updated the docs. PTAL when you have a sec. Main changes: src/retry.rs, tests/retry_tests.rs, and a one-line changelog. /cc @aj @kevin
aj: Quick q — did you keep the backoff jitter behaviour? I glanced at the impl and it looked like the default fell back to linear. can you paste the config so I can sanity check?
olivia: Good catch — I kept exponential + jitter. Added an explicit config flag and a comment. snippet: ```toml\n[retry]\nstrategy = \"exp+jitter\"\nmax_retries = 5\n``` I also added a unit test for the jitter ranges.
ci-bot: CI: unit tests ✅, lint ✅, integration: flaky on macos-12 (unrelated flaky test), build ✅. Full pipeline green-ish — rerunning the flaky job.
kevin: skimmed the diff — LGTM overall. small nit: prefer naming the const `RetryPolicy::DEFAULT` instead of `DEFAULT_POLICY` to follow the type-scoped convention. also please add a one-line changelog bullet mentioning the split.
olivia: Done — renamed const to `DEFAULT` and pushed changelog entry under docs/CHANGELOG.md (entry: "retry: introduce RetryPolicy type and config; preserve exp+jitter default"). thanks for the catch.
maria: Do we want to run a canary after merge? I have a 16:00 PT slot today and can do the smoke checks + dashboard watch. If release-bot approves slot I'll take it.
release-bot: Canary slot check: 2026-03-18T16:00:00-07:00 is available. I will run automated health checks for 30m post-deploy and notify #eng-sre on failures.
aj: Approving now. :shipit:
kevin: Approved as well provided CI finishes green and the canary goes clean.
olivia: Thanks everyone — merging after CI finishes the rerun. I'll trigger the canary and monitor the usual P95/P99 and error rates; will ping #eng-oncall if anything odd. if anyone wants the canary playbook, it's in ops/canary-runbook.md.
_notes: Thread intentionally concise and focused on PR follow-up, config confirmation, naming nit, changelog, CI, and canary scheduling.
